# Swarm catching

## Being on the list

I've been on the Teign Valley Beekeepers swarm list since 2019, for the patch between Lustleigh, Bovey Tracey and Hennock. The secretary, Pam Westaway, passes on calls from the public. Most of them are bumblebees in a bird box, or wasps, and I've learned to ask for a photo before I put the kit in the car.

## The kit box

Lives in the boot from late April to the end of June:

- Straw skep (from the association auction, 2020, £22)
- Old white sheet and a 1 m square of hardboard
- Secateurs and a small folding saw
- Water spray bottle
- Bee brush, though a goose feather is better
- Queen clip and a cardboard nucleus box with a mesh vent
- Ratchet strap, gaffer tape, a torch
- Veil, gloves, and a flask of tea, which is the most important item

## Pricing it up

I don't charge. If people offer, I suggest a donation to the association's education fund. Pam keeps a tally: in 2024 the swarm volunteers raised £340.

## The 2024 season

### 17 May, Hennock churchyard

Called at 2.15 pm by the verger, Mr Lethbridge. A big swarm hanging like a brown beard from a low hawthorn branch 1.5 m up by the lychgate. Sheet down, skep held underneath, one sharp shake of the branch. Most dropped in. Skep turned upside down on the hardboard propped on a stone so the stragglers could walk in. By 7 pm they were all inside, fanning at the gap, which means the queen is in. Picked it up at dusk and drove home with the windows down. Hived into a new box as Ivy the next morning.

### 30 May, Bovey Tracey, a garden fence

Small cast swarm, maybe 4,000 bees, on a fence post. Brushed into the nucleus box. Queen never found and they left the box the next day. Can't win them all.

### 9 June, an empty compost bin in Lustleigh

The bees had moved into the bin itself. Took the bin home whole, with permission, and moved them across onto frames on 10 June. United with Hazel on 1 July as they were queenless.

## Bait hive

An old brood box on the shed roof at 3 m height, with an old dark comb and two drops of lemongrass oil on the top bars. Put up 20 April 2024. A swarm moved in on 3 June, no work at all. Best value I've ever had from a box.

## What I've learned

1. Ask for a photo first.
2. Never climb anything. If it's more than head height, it's a job for someone younger.
3. Swarms are usually gentle, they're full of honey and have no home to defend. Still wear the veil.
4. Prevention is better: queen cells found on inspection mean an artificial swarm that week (see [[Hive inspection checklist]]).
5. Mark and note the queen in any swarm you keep, colour per year in [[Queen marking colors]].
6. Stings happen; the one in June 2024 is written up in [[Bee sting reactions]].
